newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to sell Golan land for Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel to sell Golan land for Jewish settlement.

text.p: Israel will soon begin selling land on the occupied Golan Heights in order to expand the Jewish settlement of Katzrin, a housing ministry spokesman said on Monday.
Israel's leading Peace Now movement blasted the decision as a "countdown to war" with Syria, which lost the Golan Heights to Israel in the 1967 Middle East War and demands their return.
Housing ministry spokesman Moshe Friedman confirmed media reports that land on which 96 homes are planned would soon go to market. He did not specify when tenders would be issued.
"It was decided last June to allow for natural growth of Katzrin," Friedman added.
He said Israel's northern district planning and building committee had already approved construction of the 96 homes.
The move is bound to anger Syria, which demands Israel withdraw from all of the strategic plateau in exchange for peace with the Jewish state.

"This decision will deal a great blow to the peace process. In today's tense situation, the decision to widen settlement is like a declaration of war," Peace Now spokesman Alon Arnon told Reuters, quoting a letter the group had sent to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"The beginning of work (in Katzrin) is the beginning of the countdown towards war with Syria," Arnon said.
Tensions between Israel and Syria have been on the rise since right-winger Netanyahu came to power in June with a pledge never to withdraw from the Golan.
Relations with Syria -- and all of Israel's Arab neighbours -- have deteriorated over Netanyahu's commitment to expand Jewish settlements in occupied Arab lands.
Israelis have grown jittery as the arch-foes have traded accusations of escalating tensions as each side staged military exercises on the Golan front.
Israel's previous centre-left government, ousted in May elections, said it was ready to make at least a partial pullback from the Golan in exchange for peace.
Five years of sporadic peace talks between Israel and Syria over the fate of the plateau have yet to resume under Netanyahu. Some 15,000 Jews have settled amidst 18,000 Druze on the Golan since 1967.
Israel annexed the Golan in 1981 in a move the international community does not recognise.
